story.en: Imagine Yuna is finishing dinner when a work message appears at 9:14 p.m. Her manager asks for a quick answer, but Yuna promised herself a quiet evening with her sister. Last month, a teammate who ignored late messages missed an important update. Her sister jokes that the phone deserves its own chair. Yuna must decide whether to reply now, set a boundary, or wait until morning.

page2.title: When Availability Becomes an Expectation
page2.article: Smartphones make it easy for teams to solve small problems quickly after work. That convenience can also turn availability into an unspoken expectation. Some employees feel safer replying immediately, while others protect fixed offline hours. Managers may reduce confusion by marking which messages are truly urgent. Teams also need a shared rule that does not punish people for resting. The central question is whether quick communication is worth the pressure it can create.
